drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Please find our first-turn comments to the Executive Employment Agreement. We have focused on clarifying the compensation and severance mechanics and tightening the restrictive covenant so it is more likely to be enforceable and administrable. We have left bracketed items for the business teams to confirm.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: PARTIES. This Executive Employment Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into by and between Vireo Systems Inc., a [jurisdiction] corporation (the “Company”), and [Executive Name] (the “Executive”), effective as of [Effective Date].
edits.name: Clarify parties and effective date

edits.text: 1. POSITION. The Executive shall serve as Chief Operating Officer, reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, and shall perform the duties and responsibilities customarily associated with that position and such other lawful duties as may reasonably be assigned from time to time consistent with the Executive’s position.
edits.name: Clarify role and reporting line

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of USD [●] (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to applicable withholdings. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company’s employee benefit plans and programs generally available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the terms of those plans and programs. Any annual bonus, equity award, or other incentive compensation shall be as separately approved in writing by the Company’s Board of Directors or its authorized committee.
edits.name: Clarify compensation mechanics

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, and subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims in favor of the Company, the Executive shall receive severance in an amount equal to [●] months of the Executive’s then-current Base Salary (the “Severance Amount”), payable in substantially equal installments in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Company shall also pay any earned but unpaid Base Salary through the termination date and any vested benefits required by applicable law or the applicable benefit plan terms.
edits.name: Clarify severance and release condition

edits.text: 4. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS. During employment and for twelve (12) months after the Executive’s departure, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in a Competitive Business in the Restricted Territory in a role that is the same as or substantially similar to the services the Executive provided to the Company during the final twelve (12) months of employment. For purposes of this Agreement, “Competitive Business” means a business that provides products or services that are competitive with the Company’s material products or services as of the termination date, and “Restricted Territory” means the geographic area in which the Executive had material business responsibilities during the final twelve (12) months of employment. This Section shall be enforced only to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.
edits.name: Narrow non-compete for enforceability

edits.text: Please confirm Base Salary, bonus opportunity, and any equity terms to be included here or in a separate award agreement.
edits.name: Business point: compensation details

edits.text: Please confirm the number of months for severance and whether COBRA/health benefit continuation should be included.
edits.name: Business point: severance amount

edits.text: Restrictive covenant enforceability is jurisdiction-specific. Please confirm governing law and the Executive’s expected work location so counsel can tailor this provision appropriately.
edits.name: Legal point: restrictive covenant law

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of USD [●] (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices and subject to applicable withholdings. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company’s employee benefit plans and programs generally available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the terms of those plans and programs. The Executive shall be eligible for an annual target bonus opportunity as separately approved in writing by the Company’s Board of Directors or its authorized committee (the “Target Bonus”). Any equity award or other incentive compensation shall be governed by separate award agreement(s) and applicable equity plan documents approved by the Company’s Board of Directors or its authorized committee.
edits.name: Compensation revised for target bonus / separate equity documents

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, and subject to the Executive’s timely execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims in favor of the Company in a form reasonably provided by the Company (the “Release”), the Executive shall receive: (a) an amount equal to twelve (12) months of the Executive’s then-current Base Salary, payable in substantially equal installments in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices; (b) an amount equal to the Executive’s Target Bonus for the year of termination, payable in substantially equal installments over the same twelve (12)-month severance period; and (c) if the Executive timely elects continuation coverage under COBRA or any similar applicable state law, Company-paid or reimbursed continuation coverage for the Executive and eligible dependents for up to twelve (12) months following termination, or until the Executive becomes eligible for comparable coverage from another employer, if earlier, subject to applicable law and plan terms. The Company shall also pay any earned but unpaid Base Salary through the termination date and any vested benefits required by applicable law or the applicable benefit plan terms. To comply with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code, if the period for execution and non-revocation of the Release spans two calendar years, any severance payments conditioned on the Release shall commence in the second calendar year, and payments otherwise delayed pending effectiveness of the Release shall be paid on the first administratively practicable payroll date after the Release becomes effective, subject to any additional delay required by Section 409A.
edits.name: Severance revised to 12 months base, target bonus, COBRA, and 409A release timing

edits.text:
4. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS. The Executive shall comply with the following covenants, each to be interpreted and enforced only to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law and subject to confirmation of the governing law and the Executive’s expected work location:
(a) Confidentiality. During and after employment, the Executive shall not use or disclose any confidential, proprietary, or trade secret information of the Company or its affiliates, except as required in the good-faith performance of the Executive’s duties for the Company or as permitted by applicable law. Nothing in this Agreement limits the Executive’s right to report possible violations of law to, communicate with, or participate in any investigation or proceeding conducted by any governmental agency or self-regulatory organization, or to make disclosures protected under applicable whistleblower laws.
(b) Invention Assignment. The Executive shall promptly disclose and assign to the Company all inventions, works of authorship, developments, improvements, discoveries, and other intellectual property conceived, created, developed, or reduced to practice by the Executive, alone or with others, during employment that relate to the Company’s business or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development, result from work performed for the Company, or are created using the Company’s confidential information, equipment, supplies, facilities, or resources, excluding any rights that cannot be assigned under applicable law.
(c) Customer Non-Solicitation. During employment and for twelve (12) months after the Executive’s departure, the Executive shall not directly or indirectly solicit or attempt to solicit, for the purpose of providing products or services competitive with the Company’s material products or services, any customer, client, or active business prospect of the Company with whom the Executive had material business contact or about whom the Executive received confidential information during the final twelve (12) months of employment.
(d) Employee Non-Solicitation. During employment and for twelve (12) months after the Executive’s departure, the Executive shall not directly or indirectly solicit for employment or engagement any employee or individual service provider of the Company with whom the Executive had material contact during the final twelve (12) months of employment; provided that this restriction shall not prohibit general solicitations not targeted at such persons or hiring any person who responds to such general solicitations without other prohibited solicitation by the Executive.
edits.name: Restrictive covenants revised to remove non-compete and add confidentiality, invention assignment, and non-solicits
